questions.question: In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in ________ helps in digestion of cellulose.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rumen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in the rumen (the largest compartment of the stomach) play a crucial role in the digestion of cellulose.
 
• The rumen is a fermentation chamber where complex carbohydrates, such as cellulose from plant material, are broken down by microbial fermentation.
 
• Bacteria in the rumen possess cellulolytic enzymes that break down cellulose into simpler forms that can be further digested and utilized by the ruminant host.
 
• This symbiotic relationship between ruminants and rumen bacteria allows them to efficiently extract nutrients from plant-based diets.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c75e2c157479fe2a43748fcd07a27548b2d9a6f8bfacd85ce738d3d249751e6.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Used in the production of yogurt, cheese, and other dairy products
 
 

 
 Helps in the fermentation of vegetables and pickles

 Used as a biological pesticide against insect pests
 
 

 
 Produces insecticidal toxins targeting specific pests

 Forms symbiotic relationships with leguminous plants

 Used in bioremediation to degrade environmental pollutants

questions.question: Which institution launched a list of 50 iconic Indian heritage textiles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNESCO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• UNESCO launched a list of 50 iconic Indian heritage textiles
 
• The list was titled "Handmade for the 21st Century: Safeguarding Traditional Indian Textiles​​.
 
• The list includes 50 exclusive and iconic heritage textile crafts of India. Some of these include Toda embroidery and Sungadi from Tamil Nadu, Himroo weaves from Hyderabad, and Bandha tie and dye weaving from Sambalpur in Odisha.
 
• The list documents various aspects of the textiles, including the histories and legends behind them, the complicated and secret processes behind their creation, the causes for their dwindling popularity, and strategies for their preservation​.
 
• The publication aims to address one of the major challenges to the safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage in South Asia, which is the lack of proper inventory and documentation. It brings together years of research on the selected textiles​.
 
• Some of the iconic handcrafted textiles documented from north India include Khes from Panipat, Chamba rumors from Himachal Pradesh, Thigma or wool tie and dye from Ladakh, and Awadh Jamdani from Varanasi​.
 
• From the south, textiles like Ilkal and Lambadi or Banjara embroidery from Karnataka, and Sikalnayakanpet Kalamkari from Thanjavur are included​.
 
• Textiles from other regions like Kunbi weaves from Goa, Mashru weaves and Patola from Gujarat, Himroo from Maharashtra, and Garad-Koirial from West Bengal also find a place in the list​.
 
• The UNESCO publication also functions as a sample of endangered textile crafts and includes recommendations for the protection and revitalization of these textile crafts, covering issues ranging from policy to grass-root-based micro-interventions.

questions.question: Law of Demand states that, there is a negative relationship between ________.

options.text: demand for a commodity and its supply
demand for a commodity and its price
tax on a commodity and its price
supply of a commodity and its price

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __demand for a commodity and its price__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• According to the law of demand
 
 
• ​​​​when the price of a commodity increase, the quantity demanded decreases
 
• when the price of a commodity decreases, it’s the quantity demanded increases
 
• keeping other factors remains the same.
 
 
 
• The consumer’s demand for good must be inversely related to the price of the good.
 
• There is an inverse relationship between price and demand and due to this the demand curve always has a downward slope.
 
• The demand Curve is the relation between the quantity of the good chosen by a consumer and the price of the good.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Assumptions for the Law of Demand
 
 
• ​​No change in the income of consumers 
 
• No change is the taste and preference of the consumers 
 
• No change in price related to other goods.

questions.question:
Consider the given consumption function of country X and answer the following question.

C = 100 + 0.8Y

What is the value of autonomous consumption (A) and marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in the given equation?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer** A = 100, MPC = 0.8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

The **consumption function** you provided is in the form of a **simple linear equation:**

 
• **C = A + MPC*Y**

where:

 
• **C represents consumption,**
 
• **A represents autonomous consumption,**
 
• **MPC represents the marginal propensity to consume, and**
 
• **Y represents income.**

Comparing this with your given function **C = 100 + 0.8Y, **we can identify the values of** A and MPC.**

 
• **A (Autonomous consumption)** is part of **consumption that occurs when income is zero.**
 
• It's the intercept of the consumption function on the consumption axis.
 
• This is represented by the constant term in the equation, which in this case is **100.**
 
• **MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) **is the change in consumption resulting from a **one-unit change in income.**
 
• It's the slope of the **consumption function.**
 
• In your given function, this is represented** by 0.8.**

So, in the given consumption function C = 100 + 0.8Y, autonomous consumption (A) is 100 and the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.8.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote a history of Akbar’s reign titled Akbar Nama?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Abul Fazl**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Akbarnama, which translates to Book of Akbar (1556-1605), the 3rd Mughal Emperor, was written by his court historian and biographer, Abul Fazl.
 
• It was written in Persian originally, which was the court language of the Mughals.
 
• The book includes vivid and detailed descriptions of his life and times during the reign of Akbar.
 
• It is believed it took seven years for the book to be completed.
 
• Abul Fazl was one of the Nine Jewels of the Akbar Court.
 
• The first volume of the book deals with the birth of Akbar, the history of Timur's family and the reigns of Babur and Humayun, and the Suri sultans of Delhi. 
 
• The second volume describes the detailed history of the reign of Akbar till the year 1602 and records the events during Akbar's reign.
 
• It also throws light on how Bairam Khan and Akbar won the second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu.
 
• The third volume of the Akbarnama describes the administrative system of the Empire. It also deals with Akbar's household, army, revenues, and geography of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It also provides us the information about the traditions and culture of the people living in India at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**__ ____About Abul Fazl :__​

__
 
• Abul Fazl was the grand courtier of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
 
• He was the author of the Akbarnama, the official history of Akbar's reign.
 
• Apart from Akbarnama, Abul Fazl also wrote the Persian translation of the Bible.
 
• He was also one of the Nine Jewels of the Akbar's royal court and the brother of Faizi, the poet laureate of Akbar.

Nine Jewels of Akbar:__ 

 
• The following were the Nine Jewels or Navratnas of the Akbar's Royal Court-
 
• Raja Birbal- He was a noble who won Akbar’s appreciation for his wits.
 
• Tansen-He was the musician in Akbar’s court.
 
• Abul Fazal- He was the chief advisor in the court of Akbar.
 
• Faizi- Faizi was a poet who was famous for his work Nal U Daman.
 
• Raja Man Singh- He was the General in the court of Akbar.
 
• Raja Todar Mal- He was the Finance minister in the court of Akbar.
 
• Mullah Do Piazza- Home Minister of Akbar.
 
• Fakir Aziao-Din- Religious Minister of Akbar.
 
• Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana- Defence Minister of Akbar and a renowned poet.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair regarding peninsular plateau of India is correct?

I. Central Highlands – south of Narmada river

II. Deccan Plateau – north of Narmada river
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Highlands: **The **Central Highlands **are located **north of the Narmada River. **

 
 
• They cover parts of **Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra.**
 
• This region consists of a series of **plateaus, hills, and valleys.**
 
• It is characterized by its average elevation of about **600-900 meters** above **sea level,** making it relatively higher in comparison to the surrounding plains.
 
• The** Central Highlands** are known for their rugged terrain, with prominent hill ranges such as the Vindhya Range and the Satpura Range. These ranges act as a natural boundary between northern and southern India.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau: **The **Deccan Plateau **is situated **south of the Narmada River **and covers a significant portion of **peninsular India**.
 
 
• It spans across several states, including **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.**
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** is a vast elevated region with an average height of about** 600-900 meters** above sea level, although there are certain areas where it reaches higher elevations.
 
• It is characterized by its gently rolling terrain, with extensive lava flows and volcanic activity in the past.
 
• The plateau is composed of layers of basaltic lava flows, giving rise to **black soil, **which is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Peninsular Plateau**, also known as the **Deccan Plateau**, is a large **plateau region in India**.
 
• It is located in the southern part of the Indian subcontinent and covers a major portion of the country.

questions.question: The green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about ________ percent of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When **sunlight falls **on the leaves of **green plants, a process called photosynthesis occurs**.
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the biological process by which plants convert **sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose (a form of sugar) and oxygen.** This process takes place in specialized structures within **plant cells** called **chloroplasts,** which contain a pigment called** chlorophyll that gives plants their green color.**
 
• **During photosynthesis,** **chlorophyll** absorbs the energy from **sunlight.**
 
• This energy is used to** power a series** of** chemical reactions **that convert** carbon dioxide **and **water into glucose.**
 
• **The glucose** produced is then used by the plant as a **source of energy **for various **metabolic processes, such as growth, reproduction, and maintenance of cellular functions.**
 
• However, not all the energy from sunlight can be captured and converted by plants.** Sunlight** consists of a broad spectrum of **electromagnetic radiation, including visible light.**
 
• other factors such as the angle and intensity of** sunlight, the availability of water and nutrients, and the efficiency of the plant's photosynthetic apparatus can influence the amount of energy that plants capture and convert into food energy.**
 
• On average, it is estimated that green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem are able to capture and convert approximately **1 percent **of the total energy from sunlight into food energy through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Who was conferred with the Ashok Chakra for his gallantry in 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemant Karkare.**__

• Hemant Karkare led the **ATS team** in response to the coordinated terrorist attacks that took place in Mumbai in **November 2008.**
 
• He played a crucial role in neutralizing the terrorists at various locations, including the iconic **Taj Mahal Palace Hotel.**
 
• Tragically, Hemant Karkare** lost his life in the line of duty** during the attacks while fighting against the terrorists.
 
• In recognition of his exceptional bravery and supreme sacrifice, he was posthumously** honoured with the Ashok Chakra**, India's **highest peacetime gallantry award.**

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when in ________ a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement was a major political protest in India that began in 1920 and lasted for two years.**
 
• The movement was led by **Mahatma Gandhi and was aimed at achieving independence from British rule.**
 
• The movement was successful in mobilizing a large number of people and in bringing about a number of changes, such as the repeal of the **Rowlatt Act.**
 
• However, the movement was also marked by violence, and in** February 1922, a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura, killing 22 policemen.**
 
• This incident led to Gandhi calling off the movement, as he believed that it had become violent and that it was no longer in the best interests of India.
 
• The **Chauri Chaura incident was a major setback for the Indian independence movement, but it also served as a reminder of the importance of non-violence.**
 
• **Gandhi's decision to call off the movement was a difficult one, but it was a decision that he believed was in the best interests of India.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the lenses is/are correct?

I. Power of a convex lens is represented as a positive number.

II. Power of a concave lens is represented as a negative number.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The power of a lens is a measure of its ability to bend light.**
 
• The power of a lens is **measured in diopters, and the diopter is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length in meters.**
 
• A convex lens has a** positive focal length, and a concave lens has a negative focal length.**
 
• Therefore, the power of a convex lens is positive, and the power of a concave lens is negative.
 
• **Here is a more detailed explanation of each statement:**__
 
• **Statement I:** The power of a convex lens is represented as a positive number.
 __
 
• A convex lens is a** lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges.**
 
• When light passes through a **convex lens, it is bent inward or converged.**
 
• This convergence of light rays causes objects to appear larger and closer than they actually are.
 
• The power of a** convex lens is positive because it converges light rays.**
 
 
 
• **Statement II: **The power of a concave lens is represented as a negative number.
 
 
• A concave lens is a lens that is thinner in the middle than at the edges.
 
• When light passes through a **concave lens, it is bent outward, or diverged.**
 
• This divergence of light rays causes objects to appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.
 
• The power of a** concave lens is negative because it diverges light rays.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Do not confuse between Concave/Convex Lens and Mirror__
 
• Convex lens
 
 
• The convex lens is also called a converging lens.
 
 
 
• Concave lens
 
 
• The concave lens is also called a diverging lens.
